title: Toyota Motor Corporation | Business and Management - EBSCO
content: Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi, Japan, is a leading global automobile manufacturer known for its diverse range of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and hybrids. It became the world's largest automaker in 2008 and remains a significant player in the automotive industry, employing over 370,000 individuals and producing more than 200 million vehicles since its inception. Toyota is recognized for pioneering the hybrid vehicle market with the introduction of the Prius in 1997, which was the first mass-produced hybrid automobile. The company emphasizes efficiency and innovation through its management philosophy, the Toyota Production System (TPS), which focuses on continuous improvement (kaizen) and waste reduction. Toyota's impact extends beyond manufacturing; it plays a significant role in the global economy and has strategic partnerships, such as its collaboration with Mazda. Despite facing challenges such as safety recalls, natural disasters, and the COVID-19 pandemic, Toyota has remained resilient, adapting to market demands and striving for carbon neutrality through its "beyond zero" vision in the 2020s.

title: History of Toyota

Toyota's origins lie in the Japanese weaving industry when Sakichi Toyoda invented the world's first automatic loom and, subsequently, set up the Toyoda Spinning and Weaving Company in 1918. This in turn led to the launch of the Company's first ever passenger car in 1936, the Model AA, and in 1937, the Toyota Motor Company was born. Production of Toyota vehicles outside Japan began in 1959 in Brazil and now, besides its own plants, manufacturing subsidiaries and affiliates in Japan, Toyota manufactures Toyota and Lexus brand vehicles and components throughout the world.
